fellows.name: Alexander Kiselev
fellows.bio: Moscow-born programmer and engineer who, as a fellow, worked on low-cost open-source scientific and DIY-bio lab equipment. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Andrew Hsu
fellows.bio: Left Stanford's neuroscience PhD program to found Airy Labs, an educational games startup, as a 2011 fellow (one profile lists his fellowship as 2012, but the 2011 class list and TechCrunch's May 2011 roster include him). He later co-founded Speak, the AI language-learning app, where he is CTO.

fellows.name: Ben Yu
fellows.bio: Left Harvard after one semester; as a fellow he worked on Pricemash and then co-founded Sprayable (Sprayable Energy, a topical caffeine spray, and Sprayable Sleep) with Deven Soni, developed through Start-Up Chile.

fellows.name: Christopher Rueth
fellows.bio: Fellow in information technology who co-founded Community Kit, a nonprofit building off-grid kits that provide clean water, renewable power and networked education to schools in developing communities. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Dale J. Stephens
fellows.bio: Founded UnCollege (later renamed Year On), a self-directed-learning and gap-year program, and wrote Hacking Your Education (Perigee/Penguin, 2013). Year On is listed as out of business; his current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Daniel Friedman
fellows.bio: Left Yale for the fellowship, worked at Elm City Labs and RRE Ventures, then co-founded Thinkful, the online mentor-led coding school that Chegg bought in 2019 for a reported $80M. He now co-founds Moxie, a platform that helps nurses and medspa owners launch and run their businesses.

fellows.name: Darren Zhu
fellows.bio: Yale chemistry student and iGEM synthetic-biology team member who, as a fellow, co-founded Dextro with David Luan to automate laboratory research. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: David Luan
fellows.bio: Left Yale for the fellowship and co-founded Dextro (lab automation). He went on to OpenAI and co-founded Adept AI as CEO, then ran Amazon's San Francisco AGI lab after Amazon's 2024 Adept deal, leading Nova Act. In February 2026 he announced he was leaving Amazon to start something new; no name for the venture had been found.

fellows.name: David Merfield
fellows.bio: Co-founded Tablo, a lesson-sharing tool for teachers, with Nick Cammarata during the fellowship. He has since built and runs Blot, an open-source blogging platform that publishes sites from files in Dropbox, Google Drive or Git.

fellows.name: Eden Full Goh
fellows.bio: Left Princeton for the fellowship, where she developed the SunSaluter, a low-cost solar tracker, through Roseicollis Technologies during the fellowship. After product work at Palantir and Butterfly Network she founded Mobot, which uses AI-driven mechanical robots to test mobile apps and physical products.

fellows.name: Eric McKay
fellows.bio: Arizona State economics graduate who worked with Paul Gu during the fellowship on applying market principles and data to finance, drawing on earlier data work for hedge funds and the Federal Reserve. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Faheem Zaman
fellows.bio: Fellow in economics and finance who worked on delivering health, media and financial services over mobile phones in emerging markets. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Gary Kurek
fellows.bio: Alberta inventor who founded GET Mobility Solutions to develop a powered walker-wheelchair hybrid, and is the named inventor on a motorized-walker patent (US 8,752,658, granted 2014). Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: James Proud
fellows.bio: London-born fellow who built GigLocator, then founded Hello, maker of the Sense sleep tracker (shut down 2017). He now leads Substrate, a US chipmaking startup developing X-ray lithography and its own fabs, which announced a $100M raise in October 2025.

fellows.name: Jeffrey Lim
fellows.bio: Worked during the fellowship on software for easier peer-to-peer transactions and payments, and was in the first NReduce batch. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Jim Danielson
fellows.bio: Converted a Porsche 924S to electric with a friend, and as a fellow built EV power electronics and a brushless DC motor that uses no rare-earth magnets. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: John Burnham
fellows.bio: Applied with an asteroid-mining idea and researched space technology during the fellowship, then moved into software and worked on Urbit. He co-founded Yatima/Lurk Lab, now Argument, which builds the Lurk zero-knowledge VM and proof-carrying code for Lean 4.

fellows.name: John Marbach
fellows.bio: Internet marketer who started Ingenic (human-curated content filtering) and then Glider, a smarter email client, as a fellow. A Crunchbase profile lists him as Head of Growth at Hubble Network, a satellite Bluetooth network company.

fellows.name: Laura Deming
fellows.bio: Started at MIT at 14 and left for the fellowship to work on aging research, then founded The Longevity Fund and later co-founded age1. In 2024 she unveiled Cradle, a $48M reversible-cryopreservation startup; it now operates as Until (untillabs.com), with her as CEO.

fellows.name: Nick Cammarata
fellows.bio: Left Carnegie Mellon to co-found Tablo with David Merfield during the fellowship. He became an interpretability researcher at OpenAI (co-authoring 'Zoom In' with Chris Olah) and is now at Goodfire, where in October 2026 he published 'Neural Networks Are Already Clean'.

fellows.name: Paul Gu
fellows.bio: Left Yale for the inaugural fellowship class, where he worked with Eric McKay on market-based finance ideas, and co-founded the AI lending company Upstart in 2012. After years as CTO, he became Upstart's CEO on May 1, 2026, succeeding Dave Girouard.

fellows.name: Sebastien Zany
fellows.bio: Fellow in mathematics and information technology who researched applications of category theory and type theory to software systems. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Sujay Tyle
fellows.bio: Left Harvard; during the fellowship he led business development at Scopely. He was on Hired's founding team, then co-founded and ran Frontier Car Group, which OLX/Naspers acquired in 2019. He now runs Merama, a group of Latin American e-commerce brands.

fellows.name: Tom Currier
fellows.bio: Worked on Black Swan Solar during the fellowship and co-founded Campus, a San Francisco co-living startup, in 2012. He is now founder and CEO of Maverick Power, a McKinney, Texas maker of power-distribution equipment for data centers and other mission-critical sites.

fellows.name: Anand Gupta
fellows.bio: As a fellow he worked with Tony Ho on quantitative analysis of biomedical images to help diagnose disease.

fellows.name: Charlie Stigler
fellows.bio: Developer of the Mac focus app SelfControl, who left Columbia and built Zaption, an interactive video-learning company Workday bought in 2016. After product and engineering roles at Workday he co-founded Tenor, a voice-AI platform where managers practice hard conversations (GitHub lists the org as Speaksage).

fellows.name: Chris Olah
fellows.bio: Toronto hacklab.to member who worked on ImplicitCAD and 3D printing as a fellow. He did interpretability research at Google Brain and OpenAI, then co-founded Anthropic, where he works on interpretability.
fellows.billionaireNote: Forbes real-time net worth $13.8B as of 2026-10-27 (#216 in the world); Anthropic co-founder.

fellows.name: Clay Allsopp
fellows.role: Engineering manager / PM (most recent role listed)
fellows.bio: Left Berkeley to build mobile app-creation tools (Apptory) and wrote RubyMotion books during the fellowship, then co-founded Propeller.

fellows.name: Connor Zwick
fellows.bio: Built Flashcards+, a mobile study app, and later the Coco Controller phone-gaming case during the fellowship. He co-founded Speak, the AI language-learning app, with fellow Thiel Fellow Andrew Hsu and is its CEO (from background knowledge; not re-verified this session).

fellows.name: Dylan Field
fellows.bio: Left Brown in 2012 for the fellowship to build browser-based creative tools with Evan Wallace, which became Figma. He leads Figma as CEO; the company went public on the NYSE in July 2025.
fellows.billionaireNote: Forbes real-time $1.3B as of 2026-10-27; Figma co-founder & CEO.

fellows.name: Ilya Vakhutinsky
fellows.bio: Fair Lawn, New Jersey fellow who worked on making health care more open and transparent, to lower costs and help patients make better decisions. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Jimmy Koppel
fellows.bio: Carnegie Mellon graduate who founded Tarski Technologies as a fellow to build automated program repair, then was the third employee at Apptimize. After a PhD in programming languages at MIT, he runs Mirdin, which trains professional software engineers in software design.

fellows.name: Kettner Griswold Jr.
fellows.bio: Self-taught researcher from Bethesda, Maryland who, with Paul Sebexen, co-founded Evolutionary Solutions to build a benchtop DNA/genome synthesis device during the fellowship. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Noor Siddiqui
fellows.bio: Joined the fellowship at 17 to work on human-capital and education ventures for the developing world. She founded Orchid, which offers whole-genome embryo screening for IVF patients (from background knowledge; Orchid's homepage does not name her).

fellows.name: Omar Rizwan
fellows.bio: Worked on big-data analysis during the fellowship. He has since worked at Khan Academy, Stripe and Dynamicland, and built TabFS and Screenotate. His main project now is Folk Computer, an open-source physical computing system.

fellows.name: Paul Sebexen
fellows.bio: Staten Island native who studied math at CUNY and nanomaterials at Georgia Tech, then co-founded Evolutionary Solutions with Kettner Griswold as a fellow to speed up DNA synthesis. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Ritik Malhotra
fellows.bio: UC Berkeley student and co-founder of Hackers@Berkeley who co-founded Greply, a venture-backed e-commerce and media-sharing startup, as a fellow. He now runs Savvy Wealth, a platform for independent financial advisors.

fellows.name: Ryan Lelek
fellows.bio: Ryan Lelek describes his work as cybersecurity and DevOps: building, securing and running software from cloud systems to industrial robotics. As a 2012 fellow from Schererville, Indiana, he moved to San Francisco to build simple software and hardware tools.

fellows.name: Semon Rezchikov
fellows.bio: Mathematician and Junior Professor at the Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques (IHES) since 2025, working on Floer homology and symplectic geometry; previously an NSF/Veblen Research Instructor at Princeton and the Institute for Advanced Study after a PhD at Columbia. As a 2012 fellow they built bioautomation and design tools for synthetic biology.
previous: Princeton University / Institute for Advanced Study (NSF/Veblen Research Instructor)

fellows.name: Spencer Hewett
fellows.bio: Inventor who, as a fellow, built No-Q, a system combining RFID and mobile payment to remove checkout lines and deter shoplifting. He now runs RADAR, which uses RFID and computer vision to track retail inventory.

fellows.name: Tara Seshan
fellows.role: Product Lead, Codex and ChatGPT Work
fellows.bio: Product lead for Codex and ChatGPT Work at OpenAI. Tara Seshan was previously head of product at Watershed, a climate-accounting startup, and spent about seven years at Stripe as one of its first product managers and a business lead; as a 2012 fellow she founded a health-care startup.
previous: Stripe (early product manager and business lead; Stripe Billing and Treasury)

fellows.name: Taylor Wilson
fellows.bio: Nuclear physicist based in Reno, Nevada and founder of the nuclear technology company Prometheus Industries; since 2025 he co-hosts the science podcast Giant Leap with Taylor Wilson. As a 2012 fellow he worked on detecting enriched uranium for counterterrorism and on producing medical isotopes, having built a nuclear fusion reactor as a teenager.

fellows.name: Tony Ho
fellows.bio: San Jose fellow who worked with Anand Gupta on computer vision and quantitative analysis of biomedical images. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Yoonseo Kang
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Guidebolt, a Mississauga, Ontario company building a guided decision-making and information tool for professionals on its own non-LLM AI model. Earlier they were Director of IT and CTO at Payfare, and as a 2012 fellow worked on open-source machines with Open Source Ecology.

fellows.name: Andrew Brackin
fellows.bio: Andrew Brackin, from London, joined the 2013 class at 18 to build Bunchy, a social fundraising platform. Before that he co-founded a marketplace for designers and ran Tomorrow's Web, an event for young technologists. He later ran growth at Newfront (YC W18). Crunchbase lists him as co-founder of Vial, a San Francisco drug-development company.

fellows.name: Austin Russell
fellows.bio: Austin Russell left Stanford for the 2013 class to work on compact laser-based 3D depth mapping, which became the lidar company Luminar Technologies. Luminar went public in 2020. He resigned as Luminar's CEO and chairman in May 2025 after a board ethics inquiry. His new company, Russell AI Labs, bid for Luminar in October 2025, and Luminar filed for Chapter 11 in December 2025.
fellows.billionaireNote: Briefly the world's youngest self-made billionaire after Luminar's Dec 2020 SPAC listing; Forbes 2022 Billionaires list $1.6B (as of 2022-04-05). Luminar went through Ch.11 and its equity was cancelled in 2026.

fellows.name: Christopher Walker
fellows.bio: Christopher Walker, from Chevy Chase, MD, is a video game designer, programmer and artist. He left college to start a software company and made a game designed to improve spatial cognition. As a 2013 fellow he worked on interactive software for teaching programming, music and math. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Daniel Zulla
fellows.bio: Daniel Zulla, a software engineer from Regensburg, Germany, was chosen for the 2013 class at 19 to build a secure computing architecture for servers and desktops. He was on the site's 2013 roster through January 2014 but no longer appeared by August 2014. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Darren Lim
fellows.bio: Darren Lim, from Singapore, co-founded Ractiv with Lai Xue in 2013 to build Haptix (later sold as Touch+), a sensor that turns any flat surface such as a keyboard or desk into a multitouch input; the pair met while Lim was studying in China. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Delian Asparouhov
fellows.bio: Delian Asparouhov left MIT in 2013 to develop Nightingale, a medication-reminder health app, as a Thiel Fellow. He went on to lead growth at Teespring and work at Khosla Ventures, then joined Founders Fund, where he is now a partner. In 2021 he co-founded the in-space manufacturing company Varda Space Industries, where he is president.

fellows.name: Diwank Singh Tomer
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Memory Store (MemStore, YC Spring 2026), a shared memory layer that lets a team's AI agents record and recall decisions and context across sessions. The same team earlier built Julep, an open-source agent orchestration platform; as a 2013 fellow Diwank built a collaborative learn-to-code platform.

fellows.name: Gary Le
fellows.bio: Gary Le, from East Brunswick, was a 19-year-old 2013 fellow building a real-time online identity verification system for e-commerce, online communities and sharing-economy businesses. He was listed through 2014 but did not appear on the 2015 roster. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: James Schuler
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Kafene, a New York fintech he started with Neal Desai in 2019 that offers lease-to-own financing at the point of sale for shoppers with little or no credit. Before the fellowship he went through Y Combinator in high school with Eligible; as a 2013 fellow he co-founded FundElevator, a crowdfunding platform for political campaigns and nonprofits.

fellows.name: Kevin Wang
fellows.bio: Kevin Wang, from Vernon Hills, IL, built TLDRLegal, which explains software licenses in plain English, and worked on legal and open-source licensing software as a 2013 fellow. He founded the open-source compliance and software supply-chain company FOSSA in 2015 and was its CEO until February 2026. He is now its founder and chairman.

fellows.name: Laura Ball
fellows.bio: Laura Ball, from Wauwatosa, WI, joined the 2013 class at 19 to research how neural systems assign value to information. By 2015 the fellowship site said she was writing her first novel, a satire of liberal arts colleges. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Madison (Maddy) Maxey
fellows.bio: Madison Maxey left Parsons at 18 for the 2013 class, the first fellow from the fashion industry, to work on software for garment production. She then founded The Crated, an e-textiles studio that was relaunched as Loomia, which makes flexible soft-circuit 'electronic layers'. In 2026 the Korean materials company Unichem signed an agreement to acquire all of Loomia.

fellows.name: Mark Daniel
fellows.bio: Mark Daniel, a Babson freshman from Nashville, TN, co-founded the social goal-tracking site GoalHawk in 2011. As a 2013 fellow he built StatusHawk, a status-reporting and accountability tool for companies. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Nelson Zhang
fellows.bio: Nelson Zhang, from Toronto, designed and sold hardware products in high school and college. As a 2013 fellow he worked on a desktop fabricator for electronics, meant to lower prototyping time and cost for hardware companies. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Nicky Case (listed as Nick Liow)
fellows.bio: Listed in the 2013 class as Nick Liow (18, Vancouver), working on ways to pay creators for releasing work into the public domain: Commonly.cc, whose 2013 commits are by Nicklaus Liow on Nicky Case's GitHub account (ncase). Case is now an independent creator of 'explorable explanations' such as Parable of the Polygons and The Evolution of Trust.

fellows.name: Riley Drake
fellows.bio: Riley Drake, from Baltimore, began immunology research at Johns Hopkins at 15. She left Boston College for the 2013 class to apply biophysics to broad-spectrum antiviral therapies, then turned to improving how scientific data is published and evaluated. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Riley Ennis
fellows.bio: Riley Ennis was a rising junior at Dartmouth when he joined the 2013 class to build Immudicon, a cancer-vaccine and diagnostics startup he started in high school. In 2014 he co-founded Freenome, which develops blood tests for cancer detection, and the company's site lists him as co-founder and chief product officer.

fellows.name: Ritesh Agarwal
fellows.bio: Ritesh Agarwal joined the 2013 class at 19 from India while running Oravel Stays, which he relaunched as the budget hotel chain OYO Rooms in May 2013. He is founder and CEO of PRISM, OYO's parent company. PRISM reported its first annual profit in FY2023-24 and has been preparing an IPO.

fellows.name: Thomas Sohmers
fellows.bio: Thomas Sohmers left high school in Hudson, MA, as a 17-year-old 2013 fellow to build low-power server processors, and founded REX Computing. He was later principal hardware architect at Lambda and worked on technology strategy at Groq. In 2023 he co-founded the AI inference hardware company Positron AI, which listed him as chairman in 2026.

fellows.name: William LeGate
fellows.bio: William LeGate, from Marietta, GA, taught himself to program at 14 and built more than a dozen mobile apps with over 5 million downloads. As a 2013 fellow he worked on location-based app discovery. Current work could not be verified.
previous: Imagination Research Labs (founder, iOS app studio)

fellows.name: Xinyi Chen
fellows.bio: Xinyi Chen, from Beijing, was a Princeton math major who built Helios, a low-cost telepresence prototype, at the Tigerlabs accelerator. As a fellow she moved to 3D computer vision for face detection and recognition in Chinese bank surveillance. The January 2014 site listing gives no class year for her, but the August 2014 listing, the 2015 site and a May 2013 Women 2.0 article all put her in the 2013 class. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Zach Hamed
fellows.bio: Co-founded Clay (now Mesh), a personal relationship-management app, with Matthew Achariam and was its co-CEO; Automattic acquired it in June 2025. Before Clay, Hamed led product management for Goldman Sachs' Marquee platform; as a 2013 fellow Hamed worked on tools for K-12 teachers.
previous: Goldman Sachs (led product management for the Marquee web platform)

fellows.name: Adam Munich
fellows.bio: Adam Munich, a 20-year-old inventor from Buffalo, NY, was chosen for the 2014 class to develop portable radiography technology. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Adithya Ganesh
fellows.bio: Researcher at OpenAI working on training large neural networks. As a 2014 fellow on leave from Stanford, Ganesh co-invented IntentSense, a bionic glove for partial hand amputees, and in 2018 co-founded the AI magazine The Gradient.

fellows.name: Alex Koren
fellows.bio: Alex Koren, from Bergen County, NJ, left college for the 2014 class to co-found Hyv. Hyv began as crowd-sourced supercomputing on phones and moved toward ad-free monetization tools for mobile apps. Current work could not be verified.
previous: Johns Hopkins University (left after sophomore year)

fellows.name: Ari Weinstein
fellows.bio: Ari Weinstein, an iOS jailbreak developer from Philadelphia, joined the 2014 class to build DeskConnect with fellow Conrad Kramer, then co-created the automation app Workflow, which Apple bought and turned into Shortcuts. He co-founded Software Applications Incorporated, maker of the Mac AI assistant Sky, which has announced it is joining OpenAI.

fellows.name: Benjamin Englard
fellows.bio: Benjamin Englard, from Miami, FL, is a computer scientist whose fellowship was announced by the University of Michigan's theory group. As an 18-year-old 2014 fellow he worked on combining natural language processing, computer vision and psychology to personalize technology. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Catherine (Rin) Ray
fellows.bio: Catherine Ray, now Rin Ray (they/them), earned a B.S. in computational physics from George Mason University at 16. They joined the 2014 class at 17 to apply mathematics to neuroprosthetics and other problems. They later earned a master's at UChicago and a PhD at Northwestern, and describe themselves as a researcher-artist and math postdoc at the University of Münster working where homotopy theory meets arithmetic.

fellows.name: Conrad Kramer
fellows.bio: Conrad Kramer, from Philadelphia, taught himself to program at 13 and joined the 2014 class at 17 to build DeskConnect with Ari Weinstein. He co-founded Workflow, worked on Shortcuts at Apple after the acquisition, and helped start VotePlz and the iOS Tor proxy iCepa. He then co-founded Software Applications Incorporated (Sky) with Weinstein, and Sky has announced it is joining OpenAI.

fellows.name: Eliana Lorch
fellows.bio: Eliana Lorch, from San Francisco, left home at 17 for the 2014 class to work on mathematics and neural networks. As a fellow they presented a method for visualizing deep network training trajectories with PCA at the ICML 2016 visualization workshop, and later co-authored Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP), a paper on recursively self-improving code generation published at COLM 2024. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Fouad Matin
fellows.bio: Fouad Matin, from McLean, VA, joined the 2014 class at 18 to build software that makes technical skills faster to learn. He went on to co-found StrongIntro and VotePlz, worked as an engineer at Segment, and was co-founder and CEO of the access-security company Indent from 2018 to 2024. Since May 2024 he has worked on security at OpenAI.

fellows.name: Grace Gee
fellows.bio: Grace Gee, from Port Lavaca, TX, left a joint bachelor's and master's program in computer science at Harvard for the 2014 class. She co-founded CortexML with classmate Eugene Wang to make data analysis simpler. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Ishaan Gulrajani
fellows.bio: Ishaan Gulrajani left MIT and founded a YC-backed startup that won an Apple Design Award before joining the 2014 class. He became a machine learning researcher at Facebook AI Research, Google Brain and Mila; he is a lead author of the WGAN-GP paper and a co-author of Invariant Risk Minimization. His personal site, which may be out of date, says he is a PhD student at Stanford.

fellows.name: Jarred Sumner
fellows.bio: Jarred Sumner, from Lafayette, CA, built Selfstarter, an open-source crowdfunding site, before joining the 2014 class at 18. He later created the Bun JavaScript runtime and founded Oven to develop it. Anthropic acquired Bun in late 2025, and he joined Anthropic with the Bun team. Anthropic acquired Bun in December 2025.

fellows.name: Kaushik Tiwari
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Attack Capital, a New York AI venture studio (YC W22) that builds AI software companies and gives investors access to recent YC startups. As a 2014 fellow they worked on health IT for population health management; their YC profile lists earlier work at GlucoIQ and Truedime.

fellows.name: Lucy Guo
fellows.bio: Lucy Guo, from Pleasanton, CA, left Carnegie Mellon for the 2014 class to build a multiplayer study-game platform. She later designed at Snapchat, worked at Quora, co-founded Scale AI in 2016 (leaving in 2018) and started the fund Backend Capital. Since 2022 she has been founder and CEO of the creator-monetization platform Passes.
fellows.billionaireNote: Forbes real-time $1.5B as of 2026-10-27, mostly from a ~3% Scale AI stake. Forbes named her the youngest self-made woman billionaire in 2025.

fellows.name: M. C. McGrath
fellows.bio: M. C. McGrath, from Boston, graduated from Boston University in civic technology and did research at the MIT Media Lab. As a 20-year-old 2014 fellow he ran Transparency Toolkit, a nonprofit making free software for analyzing open data on surveillance and human rights abuses. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Martin Stoyanov
fellows.bio: Martin Stoyanov, from Novi Pazar, Bulgaria, founded Emailio, an email client built around healthy email habits, after leaving high school in 2013, and was 16 when it entered Y Combinator's Winter 2014 batch. They joined the 2014 class at 17 to keep building it. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Rebecca Jolitz
fellows.bio: Postdoctoral researcher at UC Berkeley's Space Sciences Laboratory and a member of the science team for NASA's MAVEN Mars mission, studying space weather at Mars; earned a PhD in physics from the University of Colorado Boulder in 2022. As a 2014 fellow they worked on speeding up the satellite development cycle.
previous: University of Colorado Boulder (PhD in Physics, 2022)

fellows.name: Shantanu Bala
fellows.bio: Shantanu Bala, from Phoenix, AZ, joined the 2014 class at 19 to build a haptic system that turns live video and audio, such as facial expressions and sound cues, into vibrations on the skin. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Thomas Hunt
fellows.bio: Thomas Hunt, from Saratoga, CA, spent three years at the SENS Research Foundation studying Alternative Lengthening of Telomeres (ALT) in cancer. He joined the 2014 class at 17 to use high-throughput drug screening to find compounds that reduce ALT activity. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Vitalik Buterin
fellows.bio: Vitalik Buterin co-founded Bitcoin Magazine and published the Ethereum white paper in 2013. He left the University of Waterloo for the 2014 class to work full-time on Ethereum. He remains the best-known co-founder of Ethereum and a leading figure in its research.
fellows.billionaireNote: Forbes called him the world's youngest crypto billionaire (age 27) when ETH passed $3,000 in May 2021. His Forbes profile, last updated Jan 2022, shows no current net worth or list rank.

fellows.name: Caroline Beckman
fellows.bio: Named a 2015 Thiel Fellow (Sacramento, CA) as co-founder of Nomva, an organic probiotic fruit-and-vegetable snack company; she was also a founding member and VP of Special Projects at Suja Juice.

fellows.name: Cathy Tie
fellows.bio: Named a 2015 Thiel Fellow (Toronto) as co-founder and CEO of Ranomics, a genetic-variant testing startup. She later founded Locke Bio, the Los Angeles Project and Manhattan Genomics, and Wikipedia now lists her as founder and CEO of Origin Genomics.

fellows.name: George Matus
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Vector (Vector Defense), a Bluffdale, Utah company that mass-produces low-cost, expendable drones for defense customers. As a 2015 fellow they founded Teal Drones, which Red Cat Holdings acquired in 2021; they stayed on as CTO until December 2024.

fellows.name: Harry Gandhi
fellows.bio: Works on embodied cognition at Lumen Labs, a research group building physical intelligence modeled on natural systems such as swarms, fungal networks and slime molds, and helps independent researchers and deep-tech founders through 1517 Fund. As a 2015 fellow they co-founded Medella Health, which was building a smart contact lens for non-invasive health monitoring.

fellows.name: Jason Marmon
fellows.bio: Named a 2015 Thiel Fellow at 17 (Armonk, NY) for HomeSwipe, an apartment-rental search app Marmon co-founded; a 2015 Inman profile lists Marmon as its CTO.

fellows.name: Jeremy Cai
fellows.bio: Named a 2015 Thiel Fellow (Chicago, IL) as founder and CEO of OnboardIQ, software for hiring and onboarding service workers; Fountain's website footer reads 'Fountain (Onboard IQ)', suggesting the company now operates as Fountain. After co-founding the hiring platform Fountain, he founded Italic, a consumer brand selling goods straight from manufacturers.

fellows.name: Jihad Kawas
fellows.bio: Named a 2015 Thiel Fellow at 17 (Beirut, Lebanon) as founder and CEO of Saily, a mobile marketplace for buying, selling and swapping secondhand goods locally.

fellows.name: John Backus
fellows.bio: Co-founded the identity-verification company BlockScore (later Cognito) in 2014 and was its CTO; Plaid acquired Cognito in 2022. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: John Meyer
fellows.bio: Dropped out of NYU and was named a 2015 Thiel Fellow (New York, NY) as founder of Fresco News, which built newsroom tools for sourcing footage from smartphone users at breaking-news scenes.
previous: Ghost Financial (founder & CEO, 2021-2022+; fintech for ghost-kitchen operators)
Homebound (co-founder with Jack Abraham; later advisor)

fellows.name: Kieran O'Reilly
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Knot, a New York startup (founded 2019 with brother Rory O'Reilly, CEO) whose API lets banks and fintechs connect customers' cards and accounts with merchants; it raised a $10M Series A led by Nava Ventures in 2023. As a 2015 fellow they left Harvard with Rory to build GIFTY (later gifs.com), where Kieran was co-founder and CTO.

fellows.name: Liam Horne
fellows.bio: Works on Tempo, the payments-focused layer-1 blockchain for stablecoins incubated by Stripe and Paradigm. Earlier Horne introduced generalized state channels, was CEO of OP Labs (Optimism) before moving to an advisory role, and co-founded ETHGlobal and the Hack the North hackathon; as a 2015 fellow Horne was CTO of PiinPoint, location-analytics software for retailers.
previous: State channels / Web3Torrent work on Ethereum

fellows.name: Max Lock
fellows.bio: Founded Fleet (Fleet Logistics), a Portland-based digital freight forwarder, at 18 and ran it as CEO and president. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: Ocean Pleasant
fellows.bio: Named a 2015 Thiel Fellow at 17 (New York, NY) as founder of REAL Magazine, a national youth-culture publication, while developing REAL me, an app matching young people with volunteer opportunities.
previous: Real (app: 'Meet New Friends. Make an Impact.')

fellows.name: Olenka Polak
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Moetsi, a Brooklyn company offering 'Reality Modeling as a Service': real-time 1:1 digital models of physical spaces built from sensor streams, available through an API. As a 2015 fellow they co-founded myLINGO, an app that streamed synchronized foreign-language movie dubs to a phone in theaters.

fellows.name: Patrick Coughran
fellows.bio: Engineering leader at Dockwa, a marina booking platform, after leading engineering at Cambium, an AI platform for the timber industry. As a 2015 fellow they co-founded Foxtrot Systems, route-optimization software for last-mile delivery that Descartes acquired in 2022.
previous: Foxtrot Systems (co-founder & CTO; acquired by Descartes, 2022)
Cambium (VP of Engineering, c. 2024-2025; AI platform for the timber industry)
Descartes Systems Group (Senior Director, Machine Learning, from April 2022, after the Foxtrot acquisition)

fellows.name: Rory O'Reilly
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Knot, which builds a merchant-connectivity platform and API that lets financial apps and merchants link users' online accounts; co-founded it with brother Kieran O'Reilly. As a 2015 fellow they co-founded gifs.com (originally Gifyoutube), a GIF creation platform.

fellows.name: Simon Tian
fellows.bio: Named a 2015 Thiel Fellow (Montreal) as founder and CEO of Neptune, a wrist-worn mobile hardware company acquired in 2017. He now runs Fonus, a mobile virtual network operator on AT&T's network launched in 2019.

fellows.name: Stacey Ferreira
fellows.role: Director of Retail Execution and Innovation
fellows.bio: Named a 2015 Thiel Fellow (Scottsdale, AZ) as CEO of AdMoar after selling MySocialCloud; she later co-founded the gig-worker platform Forge. Wikipedia lists her at Ford as Director of Retail Execution and Innovation for Model e.

fellows.name: Zach Latta
fellows.bio: Named a 2015 Thiel Fellow at 17 (El Segundo, CA) as executive director of hackEDU, a nonprofit bringing coding clubs to high schools. He is listed as founder and executive director of Hack Club, a nonprofit network of student coding clubs.

fellows.name: Zoli Kahan
fellows.bio: Named a 2015 Thiel Fellow (Austin, TX) as CTO of Clay.io, a publisher of games for mobile web platforms.

fellows.name: Aditya Agarwalla
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Kisan Network, an online marketplace that lets Indian farmers sell produce directly to institutional buyers.

fellows.name: Alex Rodrigues
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Varden Labs, self-driving shuttles for private campuses. He went on to co-found and lead Embark Trucks, an autonomous trucking company that went public in 2021 and was acquired by Applied Intuition in 2023.

fellows.name: Anthony Zhang
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Vinovest, a platform for investing in fine wine and whiskey that StartEngine acquired in March 2026; named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Finance (2025). As a 2016 fellow they ran EnvoyNow, a campus food-delivery app started at USC and acquired by JoyRun in 2017.
previous: EnvoyNow (founder & CEO; acquired by JoyRun, Jan 2017)

fellows.name: Boyan Slat
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow as founder of The Ocean Cleanup, a nonprofit developing systems to remove plastic from the oceans; he remains its CEO.

fellows.name: Brian Truong
fellows.bio: Partner at Graph Ventures, an early-stage venture firm. As a 2016 fellow they co-founded HelloToken, a market-research alternative to display ads for digital publishers, and were its CEO from 2015 to 2017.

fellows.name: Christian Owens
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Paddle, payments, tax and billing infrastructure for software companies.

fellows.name: Cosmo Scharf
fellows.bio: Product designer and entrepreneur in XR who co-founded the VRLA expo and Mindshow (originally Visionary VR), a VR animation platform. In 2024 they co-organized Vision Hack, a global hackathon for Apple Vision Pro developers.

fellows.name: Eva Shang
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Legalist, a legal analytics platform. Legalist has since become a technology-driven investment firm focused on litigation finance and government receivables.

fellows.name: Grace Xiao
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Kynplex, communication tools for scientific labs.

fellows.name: Henry Hu
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Cafe X, automated robotic coffee bars.

fellows.name: Hunter Rosenblume
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Ordo, a K-12 school food-service company serving schools in more than 15 states, backed by Accel. As a 2016 fellow they co-founded Lunar Wireless (later Sweet), a low-cost phone carrier based in Detroit that shut down in 2020.

fellows.name: Ivonna Dumanyan
fellows.bio: Co-founded and ran Fathom AI (originally BioMetrix), a Durham, North Carolina startup making wearable sensors to predict and prevent athletic injuries; it was the 2016 fellowship project. Current work could not be verified.

fellows.name: James Boehm
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Beam, an interactive live-streaming platform for gamers. Microsoft acquired Beam in 2016 and relaunched it as Mixer.

fellows.name: James Sun
fellows.bio: Co-founded Revlo, a fan-engagement tool for Twitch streamers that Twitch acquired, and Paper, a web3 wallet and checkout company that thirdweb acquired in 2023. Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow (Canada) as co-founder and CEO of Revlo.

fellows.name: Jesse Leimgruber
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for NeoReach, influencer-marketing software for large brands, which Leimgruber co-founded and ran as CEO. NeoReach's current leadership page no longer lists him.

fellows.name: Joey Krug
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Augur, the first decentralized prediction-market platform, built on Ethereum. He co-founded Augur and later became an investor, first at Pantera Capital and then as a partner at Founders Fund.

fellows.name: Joey Levy
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Betr, a Florida-based sports betting and prediction-markets app started with Jake Paul in 2022. Earlier Levy co-founded Simplebet, a micro-betting technology company acquired by DraftKings in 2024, and as a 2016 fellow worked on the betting app Quizr after founding the fantasy-sports platform Draftpot.

fellows.name: Lexi Smith
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Carewell, a caregiving platform for families of people with dementia.

fellows.name: Luke Sophios
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for CourseKey, classroom software for career and technical schools.

fellows.name: Matt Arbesfeld
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for AppHub, tools to deploy and update mobile apps instantly. He went on to co-found LogRocket, a frontend monitoring and product analytics company.

fellows.name: Matthew Salsamendi
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CTO of All Out, a browser-based platform for making and sharing multiplayer games, aimed at games that spread through YouTube creators. Earlier co-founded the game-server host MCProHosting and Beam, the interactive live-streaming platform Microsoft acquired in 2016 and relaunched as Mixer.

fellows.name: Megan Grassell
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Yellowberry, an apparel brand making first bras for tween girls.

fellows.name: Nick Mares
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Kettle & Fire, shelf-stable bone broth from grass-fed cattle.

fellows.name: Pamela Valdés Esteva
fellows.bio: Founder of Musa, an app that helps women build meditation habits to reduce stress and support hormonal health across the menstrual cycle. As a 2016 fellow they founded Beek, which became a Latin American audiobook app with more than 4 million listeners before it shut down in February 2025.

fellows.name: Panashe Mahachi
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow (Canada) as co-founder of Lace (Lace Labs), a marketplace for cities and other municipalities to find and buy software, while a University of Waterloo math student. Lace is no longer operating. Current work could not be verified.
previous: Lace Labs (co-founder; municipal software marketplace, defunct)

fellows.name: Raul Jordan
fellows.bio: Ethereum developer who co-founded Prysmatic Labs, which built Prysm, a widely used Ethereum consensus client; Offchain Labs, the company behind Arbitrum, acquired Prysmatic Labs in 2022. As a 2016 fellow they co-founded Kynplex, communication tools for scientific labs, with Grace Xiao.
previous: Prysmatic Labs (co-founder; acquired by Offchain Labs, 2022)

fellows.name: Rohith Varanasi
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Lunar Labs, contract-free smartphones with per-app pay-as-you-go data.

fellows.name: Samuel F. Poirier
fellows.bio: Co-founded Mercantile, which builds branded small-business credit card programs for associations and banks and is now part of Onboard Partners. As a 2016 fellow Poirier was co-founder and CEO of Retinad, an analytics platform for virtual-reality apps.

fellows.name: Sohail Prasad
fellows.bio: Named a 2016 Thiel Fellow for Equidate, a secondary marketplace for private-company shares. Equidate later merged into Forge Global; he went on to co-found Destiny, which runs a publicly traded fund of private tech companies.

fellows.name: Ashish Pandhi
fellows.bio: CTO of VetraFi, a veteran-built fintech company offering a secured charge card and savings accounts to the military community. Earlier they co-founded and were CTO of Zurp, a secured-card startup that was acquired, and were the first software engineer at Runway; as a 2017 fellow they worked on Bettr, unified social-media management.

fellows.name: Colton Jang
fellows.bio: Named a 2017 Thiel Fellow while working on a machine-learning company.

fellows.name: Daria Evdokimova
fellows.bio: Named a 2017 Thiel Fellow for VoiceOps, AI that analyzes enterprise sales and support calls.

fellows.name: Dean Travers
fellows.bio: Named a 2017 Thiel Fellow for Luminopia, a virtual-reality therapy for lazy eye (amblyopia).

fellows.name: Fred Turner
fellows.bio: Named a 2017 Thiel Fellow for TL Biolabs, low-cost genotyping for livestock farmers. He went on to found Curative, which scaled COVID-19 testing in 2020 and has since become a health insurer.

fellows.name: Helson Taveras
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Keep, a Toronto company offering business banking, corporate cards and expense management to Canadian businesses, which Taveras started with Oliver Takach in 2021. As a 2017 fellow Taveras co-founded Riley (YC W17), lead qualification as a service for real-estate agents, and was its CTO.

fellows.name: Iddo Gino
fellows.bio: Named a 2017 Thiel Fellow for RapidAPI, a marketplace for finding, testing and deploying APIs. RapidAPI reached a $1B valuation in 2022 and was acquired by Nokia in 2024.

fellows.name: James Graham
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Community Phone, a home phone service that connects landline phones to cell networks instead of the internet. As a 2017 fellow they worked on Caffeine, a protocol to speed up and secure mobile app network requests.
previous: Caffeine Computing / Caffeine Software Inc. (founder & CEO)

fellows.name: Jesper Theil Thomsen
fellows.bio: Named a 2017 Thiel Fellow for SOUNDBOKS, the loudest battery-powered speaker.

fellows.name: Jordan DeCicco
fellows.bio: Named a 2017 Thiel Fellow for Super Coffee, Sunniva, maker of SuperCoffee (coffee blended with protein).

fellows.name: Jorge Izquierdo
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Tuyo, a money app offering interest-bearing USD balances, a debit card, global transfers and access to crypto and DeFi strategies. As a 2017 fellow they co-founded Aragon, a platform for creating decentralized organizations on Ethereum.

fellows.name: Lani Lazzari
fellows.bio: Founder of the skincare company Simple Sugars, which she started as a teenager; Wikipedia lists her as a 2017 Thiel Fellow. A TribLIVE profile describes her continuing to grow Simple Sugars.

fellows.name: Laura Vaughan
fellows.bio: Named a 2017 Thiel Fellow for Acorn Biolabs, Acorn Cryotech, which cryopreserves clients' stem cells.

fellows.name: Mark Prokoudine
fellows.bio: Co-founded Youtooz, a company that makes collectible figures and merchandise with YouTube and streaming creators, in 2019. As a 2017 fellow Prokoudine worked on Kickback, a Y Combinator-backed platform for competitive play and wagering in games like Minecraft, CS:GO and Dota.

fellows.name: Micah Green
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Tailos (formerly Maidbot), an Austin company that builds Rosie, a commercial robot vacuum used in hotels and other buildings. Micah Green started the company as a Cornell student after working as a hotel room attendant, and was a 2017 fellow for Maidbot.

fellows.name: Nicholas Shekerdemian
fellows.bio: Founding partner of The Venture Collective (TVC), an early-stage venture firm investing pre-seed to Series A in industrial, energy, healthcare and defense companies. As a 2017 fellow they co-founded Headstart (YC S17), a machine-learning hiring platform later acquired by Silverback United.
previous: Headstart (founder & CEO; YC S17; acquired by Silverback United)

fellows.name: Peeyush Shrivastava
fellows.bio: Named a 2017 Thiel Fellow for Genetesis, CardioFlux, a non-invasive heart magnetic-field imaging device.

fellows.name: Phat Le
fellows.bio: Founded the supplements brand Noots and ran it from 2020 to 2025, then became a product manager for AI at Eight Sleep in October 2025; Le's LinkedIn now reads 'Building Something New'. As a 2017 fellow Le co-founded Sleeker, scheduling and billing software for independent auto repair shops.

fellows.name: Prahasith Veluvolu
fellows.bio: Prahasith Veluvolu founded and ran Mimir, software for teaching and grading computer-science courses, until HackerRank acquired it in December 2019, then worked in product at HackerRank through 2023 and was head of product at CloudForge in 2024.

fellows.name: Robert Kirstiuk
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Freshline, which makes e-commerce, ordering and fulfillment software for food distributors and wholesalers. As a 2017 fellow they worked on Coastline Market, a marketplace for selling seafood before the boat lands.

fellows.name: Sam Bernstein
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Table22, a platform that lets restaurants, wine shops, bakeries and other food businesses sell subscriptions, clubs and pre-orders; it raised an $11M Series A led by Lightspeed in 2024. As a 2017 fellow they co-founded LoftSmart, a marketplace for student rentals, which pivoted to Table22 when COVID-19 made student housing unviable.

fellows.name: Shahed Khan
fellows.bio: Named a 2017 Thiel Fellow for Loom, cloud video messaging for work. Loom was valued at $1.53B in 2021 and acquired by Atlassian in 2023.

fellows.name: Sol Chen
fellows.bio: Co-founded Clara Health, a platform that matches patients with clinical trials, which M&B Sciences acquired in 2022; Chen then became chief of staff at OneSchema, a data-import software company.
previous: Clara Health (co-founder & president; acquired by M&B Sciences, 2022)

fellows.name: Tara Bosch
fellows.bio: Founder of SmartSweets, a low-sugar candy company; she used the $100,000 fellowship grant for it, and Wikipedia gives her class as 2017. TPG Growth bought a majority stake in 2020; as of 2024 she was the largest individual shareholder and a board member, and had founded Bold Beginnings, a grant program for women entrepreneurs.

fellows.name: Zaid Rahman
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Flex (formerly Flexbase), a fintech offering business owners banking, credit cards, payments and financing, which they founded in 2020 with Hadi Solh. They also co-founded the Miami early-stage fund 305 Ventures. As a 2017 fellow they built Volley, AI for personalized enterprise learning.

fellows.name: Andrew Sampson
fellows.bio: Works on 6over3 Institute, a Tokyo- and New York-based company building what it calls personal intelligence software, and maintains open-source projects including the Bebop serialization library. Andrew Sampson previously founded Rainway, the PC game-streaming platform from the 2018 fellowship, whose technology now powers Xbox Cloud Gaming according to their website.

fellows.name: André Bertram
fellows.bio: Co-founded HelpWear, a Toronto company (YC S17) making the HeartWatch, a clinical-grade ECG monitor for continuous at-home heart monitoring, and was its CEO until 2023. Bertram also co-founded Beyond Aging, a philanthropic group focused on geroscience, and joined the board of the American Federation for Aging Research.

fellows.name: Aparna Krishnan
fellows.bio: Co-founder and former CTO of Opyn, a DeFi options protocol whose seed round was led by Dragonfly Capital in 2020; current work could not be verified. As a 2018 fellow they co-founded Mechanism Labs, a grant-funded research lab on proof-of-stake and distributed consensus, with fellow members of Blockchain at Berkeley.

fellows.name: Axel Ericsson
fellows.bio: Named a 2018 Thiel Fellow (San Francisco / Stockholm) as co-founder of Vest, software that lets users earn interest on cryptocurrency held on Ethereum and other blockchains.

fellows.name: Daniel Ternyak
fellows.bio: Named a 2018 Thiel Fellow (Minneapolis, MN) as CTO of MyCrypto, an Ethereum wallet interface.

fellows.name: Divyaditya Shrivastava
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Paladin (YC S18), a Houston company whose autonomous drones launch from docks to 911 calls and stream live aerial and thermal video to first responders before ground units arrive. Divy grew up near Columbus, Ohio, and left UC Berkeley to build the company, which grew out of his 2018 fellowship project to help firefighters locate emergencies faster.

fellows.name: Erin Smith
fellows.bio: Named a 2018 Thiel Fellow (Lenexa, KS) for FacePrint, AI software that detects Parkinson's disease from facial-muscle cues; she deferred Stanford to take the fellowship. Wikipedia says she joined the venture firm Parable as an investor in 2025.

fellows.name: Gemma Busoni
fellows.bio: Named a 2018 Thiel Fellow (San Salvador / Los Angeles) as co-founder of Discovr Labs, which uses VR/AR for education and training.

fellows.name: Greg Tseng
fellows.bio: Named a 2018 Thiel Fellow (Weston, MA) as founder of Diluvian, a privacy-technology company.

fellows.name: Jamie Cox
fellows.bio: Co-founded Fluidstack in 2017 at Oxford with Gary Wu and César Maklary; the AI cloud and data-center company was reported in September 2026 to be valued at more than $18 billion. Cox also founded TreeCard (2020), a debit card that funded tree planting, which shut down in April 2026. As a 2018 fellow Cox was listed with Flare, technology to turn connected devices into cloud servers.

fellows.name: Joey Varikooty
fellows.bio: Named a 2018 Thiel Fellow (Edison, NJ) as co-founder of Amber Agriculture, which uses analytics and automation to manage, protect and market stored grain.
previous: Rockefeller University (listed as previous employer on TheOrg, role not stated)

fellows.name: Josh Sakhai
fellows.bio: Named a 2018 Thiel Fellow (Great Neck, NY) as co-founder of Ephemeral Tattoos, which was developing tattoo inks that fade on their own.

fellows.name: Joshua Browder
fellows.bio: Named a 2018 Thiel Fellow (London) as founder and CEO of DoNotPay, the 'robot lawyer' that began as an app for contesting parking tickets.

fellows.name: Julián Ríos
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Eden (formerly Eva, YC S18), a medical-imaging company whose cloud radiology platform and AI tools are used by imaging centers across Latin America; it raised a $22M Series A in 2025. As a 2018 fellow they were building Higia Technologies' EVA, a non-invasive wearable for breast-cancer risk assessment.

fellows.name: Kimberlie Le
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Prime Roots (formerly Terramino Foods), a Berkeley company that makes deli meats from koji, a fungi protein. As a 2018 fellow Le was developing fungi-based seafood and meat alternatives at Terramino Foods.

fellows.name: Liam Berryman
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Nelumbo, a Hayward, California materials company making anti-frost coatings for refrigeration and HVAC heat exchangers and PFAS-free water repellents for textiles; Kuraray acquired it in April 2025. Berryman started the company as a 2018 fellow and was part of the Cyclotron Road program.

fellows.name: Meghan Sharkus
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of ExpressionMed, a Minneapolis company that makes adhesive tapes, patches and stickers for continuous glucose monitors, insulin pumps and other diabetes devices. Sharkus started the company in 2015 as a University of St. Thomas student.

fellows.name: Robert Habermeier
fellows.bio: Named a 2018 Thiel Fellow (Bethesda, MD) as a co-founder of Polkadot; Wikipedia names him a co-creator of the Polkadot blockchain with Gavin Wood and Peter Czaban.

fellows.name: Shak Lakhani
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Avro Life Science, a biotech developing topical and transdermal drug-delivery platforms (TopiqIL, TransdermIL) for medical dermatology. Lakhani co-founded the company in 2018 and began biomaterials research at 15.

fellows.name: Tapa Ghosh
fellows.bio: Named a 2018 Thiel Fellow (Portland, OR) as founder and CEO of Vathys, which was designing machine-learning chips.

fellows.name: Adam Pollack
fellows.bio: Named a fellow for BoardRE, a mortgage startup that turned homebuyers' offers into cash offers (later operating as Accept.inc, which was acquired). He went on to leadership roles at HomeLight and is now a partner at Drive Capital investing in seed and Series A fintech, proptech and logistics startups.

fellows.name: Andrei Serban
fellows.bio: Left the University of Waterloo to build Fuzzbuzz, a YC W19 fuzz-testing-as-a-service startup that raised a $2.7M seed round.

fellows.name: Andrew Ninh
fellows.bio: Founded Docbot, a YC W19 company using computer vision to help gastroenterologists catch precancerous polyps during colonoscopy. He was founding CEO and moved to Chief Strategy Officer when Andrew Ritter became CEO with a Khosla-led Series A in 2021.

fellows.name: Claire Coder
fellows.bio: Founded Aunt Flow, which supplies free-vend dispensers and organic menstrual products to schools and businesses. She still leads the company as founder and CEO; it pivoted its supply chain to PPE during COVID-19.

fellows.name: Davis Foster
fellows.bio: Co-founded Scythe Robotics (2018-2026), maker of autonomous commercial lawn mowers, which was acquired by Autonomous Solutions Inc. (ASI) in 2026. He now co-runs Agency Tool Company (YC S26), building deployment and management infrastructure for real-world robots.

fellows.name: Emily Wang
fellows.bio: Joined the fellowship with Canairy, software that tracks chronic respiratory disease from changes in a person's cough or voice using signal processing and ML.

fellows.name: Iddris Sandu
fellows.bio: A Ghanaian-American designer and engineer who joined the fellowship to build a design and technology resource hub for African youth. He founded and leads Spatial Labs, a Los Angeles hardware/software (Web3) infrastructure company that raised a $10M seed led by Blockchain Capital with Jay-Z's Marcy Venture Partners.
previous: Design/engineering consulting (Uber, Snapchat, Instagram and others)

fellows.name: Ilayda Buyukdogan
fellows.bio: Co-founded Compocket, a Turkish hardware startup making pocket-sized, phone-connected electronics test equipment, starting with the Minis mini oscilloscope.

fellows.name: Jake Hillard
fellows.bio: Stanford EE student who founded Red Leader to build a software-defined lidar with a new digital-signal-processing architecture. CB Insights lists him as current founder and CEO of the Mountain View company, which raised $10M in 2022.

fellows.name: Jamie Marshall
fellows.bio: Left Yale to co-found Snackpass with Kevin Tan, a social food-ordering and rewards app that grew from college campuses. She is co-founder and COO; one profile dates her fellowship to 2018, but she appears in the July 2019 class announcement.

fellows.name: Joanne Peng
fellows.bio: Longevity researcher who spent the fellowship studying blood-based aging biomarkers, including work at the Buck Institute for Research on Aging. She later studied at Princeton, writes for the Institute for Progress/FAS, and her Substack lists her as Research Director at the Amaranth Foundation.
previous: Buck Institute for Research on Aging (research)

fellows.name: John Andrew Entwistle
fellows.bio: Co-founded Coder (cloud development environments) in Austin and served as CEO until 2021. He then founded Wander, a platform for booking high-end smart vacation homes, where he is founder and CEO.

fellows.name: Kai Kloepfer
fellows.bio: Started working on biometric smart guns as a teenager and founded Biofire, which in 2023 launched a 9mm handgun that unlocks only for authorized users via fingerprint and facial recognition. He leads the Colorado company as founder and CEO.

fellows.name: Matthew DiMarcantonio
fellows.bio: Was building Marble, a Williamsburg, Virginia startup making self-ordering kiosks for cashier-free restaurant checkout.

fellows.name: Mel Du
fellows.bio: Was building Ramp, a conversion kit that turns a manual wheelchair into an off-road capable electric vehicle.

fellows.name: Neiman Mathew
fellows.bio: Skipped college to spend several years at Hex Labs using AI to discover new materials. He then worked on the AI for Science fund at Schmidt Futures and invested at Amplify Partners before joining Greylock as a partner in April 2026, focused on early-stage AI founders.

fellows.name: Paige Brown
fellows.bio: Program Director at SilverLining, a climate nonprofit, where she works on its SOAR program to expand observing capacity for climate data; she now goes by Paige Brocidiacono. She co-founded WindBorne Systems and was its CEO, which earned her the Thiel Fellowship, then worked on atmospheric methane removal at Spark Climate Solutions.
previous: Spark Climate Solutions (atmospheric methane research project manager)

fellows.name: Phillip Chao
fellows.bio: Named a 2019 Thiel Fellow (Shanghai / San Francisco) for Doppler, a secrets and configuration management platform for engineering teams (YC W19). Press coverage of Doppler names Brian Vallelunga and Thomas Piccirello as its co-founders, and Chao's current role could not be verified.

fellows.name: Rohit Kalyanpur
fellows.bio: Left the University of Illinois to co-found Optivolt Labs, which began with a solar phone case and moved to shade-tolerant solar systems that let drones, scooters and robots recharge themselves. CB Insights lists him as current founder and CEO.

fellows.name: Sean Henry
fellows.bio: Dropped out of Georgia Tech to co-found Stord with Jacob Boudreau, an on-demand warehousing, fulfillment and logistics software company. He remains co-founder and CEO of the Atlanta company, valued at over $3B.

fellows.name: Tieshun Roquerre
fellows.bio: Left MIT to found Namebase, a registrar and exchange for Handshake decentralized domains that was sold to Namecheap in 2021. As the pseudonymous "Pacman" he co-founded the NFT marketplace Blur and is listed as founder of the Blast blockchain.

fellows.name: Will Manidis
fellows.bio: Joined the fellowship with Cascade.bio, a tool for biomedical researchers to find and share technical information, and went on to found ScienceIO, a healthcare language-model company. His bio says ScienceIO was sold to a large EMR provider, where he now runs AI projects.

fellows.name: Aaron Hannon
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Luminate Medical (YC S21), a Galway, Ireland company that developed Lily, a device to prevent chemotherapy-induced hair loss now in US clinical trials, and also offers nurse-led cancer infusion care at home. It raised a €15M Series A in 2024.

fellows.name: Adam Guild
fellows.bio: Joined the fellowship with Profitboss, online ordering and marketing software for independent restaurants. The company became Owner (owner.com), where he is co-founder and CEO.

fellows.name: Ben Stern
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Tenkara, a startup building AI agents that automate back-office operations for US manufacturers, such as supplier discovery, procurement and freight; it raised $7M led by True Ventures in 2026. Stern previously founded Nohbo, a maker of water-soluble single-use shampoo and soap drops, which won a Shark Tank deal with Mark Cuban.

fellows.name: Blake Resnick
fellows.bio: Founded BRINC after the 2017 Las Vegas shooting to build drones for police and tactical teams in barricade, hostage and active-shooter situations. He is founder and CEO; BRINC says its products are used by over 900 public-safety agencies and has a Seattle headquarters.

fellows.name: Brandon Wang
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CTO of AIUC (the Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company), which writes the AIUC-1 security and safety standard for AI agents and pairs audits with liability insurance; it came out of stealth in July 2025 with a $15M seed led by Nat Friedman. As a 2020 fellow they were building Dreambound, planning tools and financing for workforce-training courses.

fellows.name: Brian Gu
fellows.bio: Created Dark Forest, a decentralized real-time strategy game on Ethereum that uses zkSNARKs. His public GitHub profile (gubsheep) lists 0xPARC, the Ethereum application R&D group.

fellows.name: Dylan Diamond
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Saturn, a social calendar app for high school students that Snap acquired in June 2025 and kept running as a standalone service. Diamond started it at Staples High School in Connecticut and launched it with Max Baron while at the University of Pennsylvania.

fellows.name: Griffin Barnicutt
fellows.bio: Was building Palitronica, which detects compromised parts in supply chains and monitors critical infrastructure and military systems for cyberattacks and tampering.

fellows.name: Ignacio Belieres Montero
fellows.bio: Founded Epic Aerospace (YC S19), building orbital transfer vehicles for last-mile satellite delivery. Its first space tug, CHIMERA LEO 1, launched on SpaceX's Transporter-6 mission.

fellows.name: Jasmine Wang
fellows.bio: Named a fellow while working on Copysmith, an AI service that turns keywords into marketing copy, and writing a speculative-fiction novel.
previous: Co-author, What Makes Us Human: An Artificial Intelligence Answers Life's Biggest Questions (Sounds True, 2022, with Iain S. Thomas)

fellows.name: Joseph Kitonga
fellows.bio: Kenyan-born founder who left Penn State with the fellowship to start Vitable Health (YC S20), offering hourly workers affordable primary and urgent care. He is still founder and CEO of the Philadelphia company.

fellows.name: Kenta Iwasaki
fellows.bio: Was building Hyperia, a decentralized virtual power plant that traces and distributes renewable energy to households and businesses.

fellows.name: Lyn Chen
fellows.bio: Co-founder and instructor of Cansbridge Scholars, a community and program that runs cohort-based courses, such as an 8-week Foundations course, for ambitious young people. Previously co-founded LayerCI (later webapp.io, YC S20), a CI/CD and preview-environment platform that was acquired.

fellows.name: Margaret Nyawira Karaba
fellows.bio: Kenyan founder of Nurture and Reset, which sells moringa teas and powders sourced from partner farmers paid fair wages.

fellows.name: Michael Broughton
fellows.bio: Left USC to co-found Perch, later renamed Altro (YC S20), which let people build credit from rent and subscription payments. Altro's site now carries a letter from him and co-founder Ayush Jain saying the company has been acquired.

fellows.name: Michael Chime
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Prepared, AI software for 911 call-takers and dispatchers, which Axon agreed to acquire in September 2025; Prepared now forms the intelligence layer of Axon 911. They left Yale for the fellowship to build Prepared, which began as a school safety app.

fellows.name: Phoebe Yao
fellows.bio: Founder of Pareto, which supplies expert human data and evaluation research for training AI models. Pareto began as a remote-work bootcamp for women and became a virtual-assistant service during the pandemic before shifting to AI training data.

fellows.name: Robbie Ferguson
fellows.bio: Co-founded Immutable (formerly Fuel Games) in Sydney with James Ferguson and Alex Connolly. The company makes Gods Unchained and the Immutable X Ethereum layer-2 for blockchain gaming.

fellows.name: Scott Fitsimones
fellows.bio: Co-founded AirGarage, a parking-lot management and operations company handling enforcement, payments and visitor registration, which raised a round led by a16z. His GitHub profile still lists him as a co-founder.

fellows.name: Shane Curran
fellows.bio: Won Ireland's BT Young Scientist award in 2017 for qCrypt, a post-quantum encrypted storage project. He founded Evervault, a Dublin company building encryption infrastructure for developers that expanded into payments security in 2024.

fellows.name: Sheridan Clayborne
fellows.bio: Entered Northwestern at 15 and left to co-found Lendtable (YC S20), which advanced employees cash so they could capture their full 401(k) match and ESPP.

fellows.name: Stephanie Mills
fellows.bio: Was building CodeGem, which plugs into engineering workflows to analyze a software team's productivity, collaboration and engagement.

fellows.name: Thomas Suarez
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Raven Resonance, a San Francisco lab building Raven Prism, all-day AR glasses that run its own Linux-based RavenOS. Previously co-founded Teleportal, an AR and 3D creator-tools startup, and led its engineering for seven years.
previous: Georgia Tech Contextual Computing Group (wearable computing research)

fellows.name: Toni Oloko
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Dandy, a New York dental technology company started in 2018 with Wharton classmate Daniel Hanover that provides digital lab and manufacturing services to dentists. Earlier, as a Boston high-school student, Oloko built the PracticeGigs app.

fellows.name: Alex Taylor
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Orb Aerospace, which is building autonomous aircraft, from 10-pound drones to 3,000-pound planes, as infrastructure for a humanitarian air force. Taylor started Orb at 16 and joined the fellowship with it.

fellows.name: Alfonso de los Rios
fellows.bio: Founded Nowports (YC W19), a Monterrey-based digital freight forwarder that handles import and export logistics for Latin American companies. He is listed as founder and CEO. (Class announced Jan 6, 2022; sometimes called the 2021 cohort.)

fellows.name: Ana Cornell
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Acorn Genetics, a Chicago company that makes SENTRI, a compact molecular detection device, and is developing a portable solid-state nanopore DNA sequencer. The company began at Northwestern as GenomeLock, a privacy-focused at-home DNA test.

fellows.name: Ariana Sokolov
fellows.bio: Was developing more affordable tools and testing for neurodiverse people (ADHD, dyslexia, mild autism). (Class announced Jan 6, 2022; sometimes called the 2021 cohort.)

fellows.name: Ben Botvinick
fellows.bio: Founded Hyper (YC S21), which let anyone launch an online business and sell memberships (e.g. to Discord servers) with payments built in. hyper.co now redirects to Whop, and his personal site says he is studying history at Stanford. (Class announced Jan 6, 2022; sometimes called the 2021 cohort.)

fellows.name: Ben Nashman
fellows.bio: Started exploring low-field magnetic resonance spectroscopy in high school and founded Synex Medical to build non-invasive health monitoring, starting with a needle-free glucose monitor. He leads the Toronto company as founder. (Class announced Jan 6, 2022; sometimes called the 2021 cohort.)

fellows.name: Dayton Mills
fellows.bio: Co-founder of One Big Sip, a small self-funded indie game studio whose first title is the PC action roguelite We Steal From Old People: The Game. Previously co-founded and led Branch, the Seattle web3 game studio behind Castaways, the company Mills joined the fellowship with.

fellows.name: Edward Beccle
fellows.bio: Entrepreneur on the board of Beyond Type 1, the type 1 diabetes nonprofit, since January 2024. He co-founded Glorify, a Christian daily worship and devotional app, in 2019 and was its co-CEO with Henry Costa.
previous: Hintsa / GraspHR (co-founder; TechRound says he co-founded Hintsa, a high-performance coaching platform, in 2017 and sold it)

fellows.name: Geffen Avraham
fellows.bio: Launched his first satellite at 18 and created Skyline Celestial to build a "personal computer of satellites" that opens space to individuals. (Class announced Jan 6, 2022; sometimes called the 2021 cohort.)

fellows.name: Ian Lee
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Nexor, a San Francisco startup building AI agents that call, text and email leads to book meetings and close sales; it went through a16z's Speedrun accelerator in 2026. Before that Ian Lee co-founded Examedi (YC S21), a Latin American at-home healthcare marketplace, and led it as CEO until late 2024.
previous: Examedi (co-founder & CEO until Oct 2024; left day-to-day management Jan 2025)

fellows.name: James Dacombe
fellows.bio: Founded CoMind, a London neurotechnology company developing non-invasive neuroimaging and brain-monitoring tools. He is founder and CEO. (Class announced Jan 6, 2022; sometimes called the 2021 cohort.)

fellows.name: John Ciocca
fellows.bio: Founder of Purple, a startup building financial products that help people with disabilities save; Ciocca joined the fellowship with it.

fellows.name: Kiara Nirghin
fellows.bio: South African Google Science Fair grand-prize winner who joined the fellowship with Rather, a fintech for net-worth-building assets. She co-founded Chima (YC W23) with her sister Nikhara, building AI infrastructure to help large companies customize models on their data, and serves as CTO. (Class announced Jan 6, 2022; sometimes called the 2021 cohort.)

fellows.name: Lada Nuzhna
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of General Control, a biotech startup engineering programmable epigenetic medicines for age-related diseases, which announced a platform partnership with Novo Nordisk in November 2025. Born in Avdiivka, Ukraine, they left Northwestern for the Thiel Fellowship and co-founded Impetus Grants, which has funded about $34M of aging research.
previous: Impetus Grants (co-founder; longevity research grants, now run by Norn Group)
Northwestern University (physics & computer science, left for the fellowship)

fellows.name: Michael Lee
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Biodock (YC W21), an Austin-based company whose cloud AI platform automates analysis of microscopy images; previously a deep learning researcher at Stanford and a co-author of the CellSeg nucleus-segmentation tool.
previous: Stanford University (deep learning researcher; co-author of CellSeg, Nolan Lab)

fellows.name: Nastassia Ponomarenko
fellows.bio: Founder of Corecircle, a social fitness and workout-tracking iOS app (published by Connectful LLC) that passed 200,000 users in 2022. Ponomarenko earlier built Connectful, a networking app for Gen Z, and was a fitness creator who launched an apparel brand at 18.

fellows.name: Oliver Edholm
fellows.bio: Joined Klarna as an AI researcher at 15 and founded Depict (YC S20), a Stockholm e-commerce merchandising and recommendation platform that raised $17M. (Class announced Jan 6, 2022; sometimes called the 2021 cohort.)

fellows.name: Rachel Xu
fellows.bio: Was building blockchain tools that let artists and creatives own their IP and profits autonomously. (Class announced Jan 6, 2022; sometimes called the 2021 cohort.)

fellows.name: Raina Jain
fellows.bio: Founder of Queen Bee, which sells cold-pressed wellness shots such as ginger turmeric and fire cider; former NFL quarterback Tyrod Taylor is a co-founder. Queen Bee grew out of HiveGuard, a device against Varroa mites that Raina Jain started building in high school, and she left UConn for the fellowship.
previous: HiveGuard (beehive mite-control device, high school project)

fellows.name: Ryan Park
fellows.bio: Was building Anchor, a DeFi savings protocol offering stable yields on stablecoin deposits funded by proof-of-stake block rewards. (Class announced Jan 6, 2022; sometimes called the 2021 cohort.)

fellows.name: Tamara Chayo Romo
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of MEDU Protection, a Mexican company that makes and sells reusable, antiviral medical gowns that can be washed up to 50 times; named to Forbes Mexico's 30 Under 30 in 2025. Started MEDU during the COVID-19 pandemic while studying chemical engineering at Universidad La Salle Mexico.
previous: Universidad La Salle Mexico (chemical engineering, left)

fellows.name: Tejas Manohar
fellows.bio: Former early Segment engineer who co-founded Hightouch (YC S19), a reverse-ETL and composable CDP platform that syncs warehouse data into business tools like Salesforce and HubSpot. He remains a co-founder. (Class announced Jan 6, 2022; sometimes called the 2021 cohort.)

fellows.name: Tyler Bernstein
fellows.bio: Co-founded Zeno Power, which grew out of a 2017 Vanderbilt project and builds small radioisotope power systems to provide reliable power in remote and austere environments. He remains a co-founder. (Class announced Jan 6, 2022; sometimes called the 2021 cohort.)

fellows.name: Akshaya Dinesh
fellows.bio: Runs Spellbound, a no-code platform that lets marketing teams embed interactive elements such as carts, surveys and forms directly inside emails.

fellows.name: Alex Singer
fellows.bio: Founder of Voldex, a game studio that builds and acquires titles on Roblox and Minecraft, including Brookhaven and Driving Empire; a16z led its Series A in 2023.

fellows.name: Ethan Thornton
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Mach Industries, a Huntington Beach defense manufacturer building low-cost aerospace and defense systems at scale; it bought rocket-propulsion firm Exquadrum for $50M.

fellows.name: Hugo Chrost
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Solvemed, which makes the PuRe smartphone-based pupillometer and other AI tools for objective neurological assessment with hospital EMR integration.

fellows.name: Ian Michael Brock
fellows.bio: Founder of Dream Hustle Code, a Chicago nonprofit introducing Black and Brown youth to computer science through coding leagues, virtual field trips and a workforce pipeline into tech.

fellows.name: Jake Adler
fellows.bio: Founder of Pilgrim, a defense-focused biotech whose flagship Kingsfoil is a hemostatic wound dressing; it raised a roughly $4.3M seed led by Cantos with Thiel Capital participating. He was selected with the sleep-neurostimulation project Neusleep.

fellows.name: John Guibas
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Succinct, which builds zero-knowledge proof infrastructure including the SP1 zkVM and the Succinct Prover Network.

fellows.name: John McElhone
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of CropSafe, a Northern Irish agtech company that uses satellite imagery and machine learning for crop monitoring, farm banking and production forecasting.

fellows.name: Kai Micah Mills
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Cryopets, which offers whole-body cryopreservation for pets alongside veterinary care, now headquartered in San Antonio, Texas.

fellows.name: Kesava Kirupa Dinakaran
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Luminai (originally DigitalBrain, YC 2020), an AI automation platform for health-system operations that reported a $38M Series B in 2026 (per secondary profiles).

fellows.name: Kian Sadeghi
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Nucleus Genomics, a New York consumer genetics company offering whole-genome health testing and IVF embryo analysis; raised a $14M Series A in 2025.

fellows.name: Markie Wagner
fellows.bio: Founder of Delphi Labs, described as a research and advisory firm on applied AI and frontier technology; no newer venture was found.

fellows.name: Michael Ioffe
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Arist, which began as SMS/Slack/Teams microlearning and now sells AI agents that interview employees and analyze data to diagnose organizational bottlenecks.

fellows.name: Nik Shevchenko
fellows.bio: Founder of Omi (Based Hardware Inc.), a San Francisco company making an open-source AI wearable pendant that records conversations and turns them into summaries and to-dos. Earlier founded WeLoveNoCode, a no-code developer marketplace that Toptal acquired in 2023.

fellows.name: Quinn Favret
fellows.bio: Co-founder and COO of Tavus, a 'human computing' company that builds real-time conversational AI video agents, started with CEO Hassaan Raza.

fellows.name: Reiss Jones
fellows.bio: Founder of Daydream Labs. As a 2023 fellow Jones worked on Macro Energy, a project to build a cheap, accessible carbon-negative energy source.

fellows.name: Samarth Athreya
fellows.bio: Named in the 2023 class for Axiome, a Burlington, Ontario startup developing single-molecule electronic biosensors for drug discovery and point-of-care diagnostics.

fellows.name: Sara Du
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Ando, a Slack alternative built for teams of humans and AI agents that came out of stealth in September 2026 with $20M from Accel, Index and Emergence.

fellows.name: Sonny Mo
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Bloom, a YC-backed investing app for teens and young adults with custodial brokerage accounts and built-in financial education.

fellows.name: Victor Cardenas
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Slash, a business banking platform (accounts, corporate cards, payments, crypto) that raised a $100M Series C at a $1.4B valuation in April 2026.

fellows.name: Adarsh Hiremath
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Mercor, the AI hiring and expert-data marketplace that supplies human expertise to AI labs; Forbes counted him among the youngest self-made billionaires in 2026.
fellows.billionaireNote: Forbes real-time $2.2B as of 2026-10-27; Mercor co-founder.

fellows.name: Alexandra Debow
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of SWSH, a shared-album app that has become a fan-engagement platform collecting photos and videos at live events; it announced a $4M seed round.

fellows.name: Augustus Doricko
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Rainmaker, an El Segundo company that uses drones and radar to seed clouds with silver iodide to increase precipitation in the drought-prone American West.

fellows.name: Brendan Foody
fellows.bio: Co-founder and co-CEO of Mercor, which uses AI vetting to match experts with AI labs and companies; the three Mercor founders became billionaires in 2025-26.
fellows.billionaireNote: Forbes real-time $2.2B as of 2026-10-27; ~22% of Mercor. Became one of the world's three youngest self-made billionaires in Oct 2025 when Mercor hit $10B.

fellows.name: Charlie Wu
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Orchard Robotics, which mounts cameras on farm equipment and uses AI to map fruit, growth, yield and crop health; it raised a $22M Series A in 2025.

fellows.name: Christopher Zhu
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Etched, which designs Sohu, a transformer-specific AI inference ASIC.

fellows.name: Diogenes Casares
fellows.bio: Argentine crypto builder who launched the Stream Protocol trading platform in 2024 (shut down that November and later sold, before the separate Stream Finance collapse); now listed as founder of Klyra, a multi-exchange trading platform.

fellows.name: Felipe Meneses
