fellows.bio: Co-founded Decade, a São Paulo AI wealth-management startup, with former Nubank CTO Vitor Olivier; it announced an $85M seed round from Greenoaks, Benchmark and Diffusion in August 2026. He previously co-founded Hyperplane, which Nubank acquired in 2024.

fellows.name: Gavin Uberti
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Etched, the maker of the Sohu transformer ASIC; it raised a $120M Series A in June 2024 to fabricate its first chips at TSMC.

fellows.name: Govind Gnanakumar
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Automorphic (YC S23), which builds a platform for continuously fine-tuning and improving custom language models; YC still lists the company as active.

fellows.name: Jacob Rodriguez
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Oligo Space, which automates spacecraft design and manufacturing; its first spacecraft, Chimera-1, was slated for SpaceX's Transporter-15 rideshare.

fellows.name: Joseph Semrai
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Context, an AI-native office suite that reasons across documents, spreadsheets and presentations; it raised an $11M seed led by Lux Capital in 2025.

fellows.name: Luke Farritor
fellows.bio: Won the 2024 Vesuvius Challenge grand prize with his team for using AI to read Herculaneum scrolls, then joined DOGE in 2025 and worked across GSA, HHS, Energy and other agencies. In 2026 he co-founded Cathedral with three other former DOGE staffers: an AI cybersecurity startup for the U.S. military that raised $160M at a $1.4B valuation in July 2026.

fellows.name: Pavel Asparouhov
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Silna Health, which automates prior authorizations, benefit checks and insurance monitoring for healthcare providers; it raised about $27M across seed and Series A rounds from Accel and Bain Capital Ventures.

fellows.name: Peter Hansen
fellows.bio: Named in the 2024 class for Januus, a London crypto-intelligence startup mapping crypto wallets to real-world people and locations; his current role was not confirmed.

fellows.name: Robert Wachen
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Etched, which builds transformer-specific AI inference chips (Sohu).

fellows.name: Surya Midha
fellows.bio: Co-founder and board chairman of Mercor, the AI-driven talent and expert-data marketplace; Forbes reported him as one of the world's youngest self-made billionaires.
fellows.billionaireNote: Forbes real-time $2.2B as of 2026-10-27; Mercor co-founder.

fellows.name: Tarun Amasa
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Endex, which builds autonomous AI financial-analyst agents that work inside Excel; it raised $14M led by the OpenAI Startup Fund in 2025.

fellows.name: Walden Yan
fellows.bio: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer of Cognition, the applied AI lab behind the autonomous AI software engineer Devin.

fellows.name: Yash Patil
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Applied Compute, which trains custom models for enterprises with reinforcement-learning post-training on their own data; customers include DoorDash, Mercor and Harvey.

fellows.name: Aidan Smith
fellows.bio: Building Innerphases, which develops 'human-native' communication devices meant to change how people work and think.

fellows.name: Carlo Kobe
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Mine (formerly Fizz, YC S21), a personal finance app for young adults built around a credit-building debit card and MoneyGPT, an AI money assistant; the company rebranded and raised a $14M Series A led by 359 Capital in January 2026. Originally from Hamburg, Germany, Kobe left Harvard to build the company.

fellows.name: Colton El-Habr
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Orbit Technologies, which builds non-invasive, behind-the-ear vestibular neurostimulators aimed at sleep, metabolism and other autonomic functions. They co-founded Orbit with fellow Steven Pang in 2023 and left Johns Hopkins to work on it full-time.

fellows.name: Elias Fizesan
fellows.bio: Building Canopy Labs, which develops foundation models for digital humans meant to be indistinguishable from real people.

fellows.name: Fabian Gruber
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CPTO of Manex AI, a Munich company whose Kosmos agent-orchestration platform automates quality and production work for manufacturers such as BMW, Audi and Stellantis.

fellows.name: Ferdinand Dabitz
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Augustus, the 'Global Dollar Bank', a clearing bank that gives international fintechs and banks direct access to dollar accounts and payment rails; it received a conditional OCC national bank charter in May 2026 and raised a $180M Series B at a $1B valuation led by Tiger Global in July 2026. The company, founded in 2022, was known as Ivy when Dabitz joined the 2025 fellowship class.

fellows.name: Hooman Reza Nezhad
fellows.bio: CEO of Solcoa Industries, an Alameda, California company that produces rare earth metals (neodymium-praseodymium and samarium-cobalt) with an in-house chemistry and reactor process; in September 2026 it announced $75M ($45M equity led by Bain Capital Ventures plus $30M debt anchored by J.P. Morgan) to build Solcoa One, a 500-tonne-per-year plant in Nevada.

fellows.name: Jackson Denka
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Azura, a zero-fee onchain trading platform for crypto, tokenized equities, commodities and memecoins priced in USD; Azura raised a $6.9M seed round led by Initialized Capital when it launched publicly in October 2024. Its predecessor, Thunder, was an invite-only trading beta for professional traders.

fellows.name: Jennifer Lin
fellows.bio: Named in the 2025 class for an unnamed startup giving rare-disease patients faster access to new therapies with clear signs of efficacy.

fellows.name: Juan Ebrath
fellows.bio: Building Phase, a South San Francisco research lab in stealth developing bioelectronic interfaces to regenerate the human body, aiming to repair failed organs and regrow amputated limbs.

fellows.name: Koki Mashita
fellows.bio: Building Aeolus, a San Francisco company making hardware and software to reduce weather risk, starting with products to mitigate hurricanes and severe storms ('planetary defense for extreme weather').

fellows.name: Sigil Wen
fellows.bio: Building Conway Research, an AI lab focused on efficient on-device models and fast inference, whose first product, Underdog, is a personal AI that runs locally on a Mac. He wrote the 'Web 4.0' essay (Feb 2026) and founded the O-1/EB-1A visa company Extraordinary.

fellows.name: Soren Monroe-Anderson
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Neros, a U.S. maker of low-cost FPV, autonomous and interceptor military drones at high volume; Neros announced a $250M Series C at a $2.5B valuation.

fellows.name: Steven Pang
fellows.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Orbit Technologies, which builds non-invasive, behind-the-ear vestibular neurostimulators aimed at sleep, metabolism and other autonomic functions. They co-founded Orbit with fellow Colton El-Habr in 2023 as a Georgetown computer science student.

fellows.name: Teddy Warner
fellows.bio: Founder and CEO of Intempus, which aims to give robots emotional intelligence so their behavior is more predictable and easier to read; he lists himself as Intempus founder and CEO.

fellows.name: Alex Shieh
fellows.bio: Founder of The Antifraud Company, which combines AI and investigative journalism to find fraud against U.S. taxpayers; he testified to Congress on government fraud in June 2025.

fellows.name: Antoni Kiszka
fellows.bio: Warsaw-based founder of Derpetual, which builds leveraged 'abstract futures' markets on measurable quantities beyond traditional assets.

fellows.name: Aubrey Niederhoffer
fellows.bio: Building Swoop, which bills itself as Africa's super app and runs same-day food delivery in Lagos (Yaba) and in Eswatini, with groceries and pharmacy listed as coming soon. They left UC Berkeley's Haas School of Business to move to Nigeria for it, after several years running businesses in Southern Africa.

fellows.name: Claire Wang
fellows.bio: Building biologically accurate simulations of entire nervous systems, starting with C. elegans, as groundwork for brain-computer interfaces; she left MIT for the fellowship. The official release names no company; 'Bioneural Lab' comes from RichNerds.
previous: MIT Jasanoff Lab (C. elegans whole-brain simulation research)

fellows.name: Galen Mead
fellows.bio: Co-founder of Standard Intelligence, a small San Francisco AI lab that pretrains models to learn from the internet, including the hertz-dev speech model and FDM-1, a general computer-action model; the lab raised $75M from Sequoia and Spark Capital in April 2026.

fellows.name: Harry O'Connor
fellows.bio: Founder of Sentient Machines, a research lab building robotics foundation models that generalize across tasks and environments; he is a two-time BT Young Scientist winner and an Emergent Ventures fellow.

fellows.name: Ishan Gupta
fellows.bio: Co-founder (with David Paffenholz) of Juicebox (YC S22), an AI recruiting platform that searches 800M+ profiles by skills; it has closed a Series B.

fellows.name: Kyler Wang
fellows.bio: Building Action, an AI company in stealth. He is a Stanford CS student who was a member of technical staff at OpenAI (agent memory) and an early engineer at Mercor.

fellows.name: Milan Lustig
fellows.bio: CEO of Spring Silicon, announced as Opt32 (opt32.com now redirects there): a Brooklyn company building compilers, kernels and silicon to run ML models onboard robots, cars and drones. He is on leave from Harvard.

fellows.name: Nick Dobroshinsky
fellows.bio: Founder of EveryTicker, which publishes AI-assisted, fundamentals-focused research on all 5,000+ U.S. stocks, including the many with no analyst coverage; he started it as a teenager.

fellows.name: Samuel Carvalho
fellows.bio: Building Praso, wholesale-commerce infrastructure (procurement, credit lines and workflow tools) for small businesses in underserved parts of Brazil, based in Recife; reported to have raised $14.5M.

fellows.name: Victor Boyd
fellows.bio: Co-founded Cavalla, which aims to deliver anything anywhere in under five hours, starting with autonomous forklifts and building toward hypersonic logistics; CEO Mohammad Nafisi is his co-founder.
